scores.evidence: Database replication on-prem→cloud is **async**, using change data capture (CDC).
scores.rationale: Mechanisms (CDC, fencing, reverse CDC, SIU/ADT, NIST 800-88) are accurate; minor issues like managed DB with reverse CDC via DMS, "Monday 08:00 peak" lag claim, and replay against clone are plausible but not fully qualified.

scores.evidence: No unplanned outage, and staff never lose the ability to *view* schedules. At the one moment the database writer switches over, new bookings pause for up to 60 seconds.
scores.rationale: Interprets zero-downtime sensibly and honestly, covers core needs and defers scope explicitly, though vendor support and cutover communication/hypercare are thin.

scores.evidence: the on-prem app's write permission is revoked at both the routing layer *and* the database, so the two sides can never both accept writes.
scores.rationale: Single write authority, consistent fencing, rollback and sync/async choices are applied consistently across phases; no contradictions found.

scores.evidence: Replay a week of captured production write requests against a *cloned snapshot* of the cloud database, never the live replica.
scores.rationale: Validation targets specific risks (shadow compare, checksums, rule checks, rehearsals, rollback drill) early via Phase 0 and continues post-cutover, though some thresholds are stated without justification.

scores.evidence: Assumptions to confirm in week 1. These can change the plan:
scores.rationale: Key assumptions and revisit triggers are explicit, but numeric targets (60 s, 99.99%, 5 s) are presented as defaults with limited basis.

scores.evidence: Worst failure: Split-brain. Both the old and new databases accept bookings at the same moment
scores.rationale: Split-brain, PHI leak, lag, hidden dependencies, rollback triggers covered concretely; WAN/cloud outage clinical downtime handling and adversarial input are lighter.

scores.evidence: Written runbook, with a timed step for each action and named owners.
scores.rationale: IaC, dashboards, alerts, rollback and ownership are addressed; incident response/on-call and ongoing ops team sizing are thin.

scores.evidence: Cost optimisation (reserved capacity, right-sizing). Pull forward after 60 days of steady usage data.
scores.rationale: Cost is essentially deferred with no estimates, drivers (dual-running, egress, DR, links), or controls.

scores.evidence: Keep it as a permanent switch. Remove it only if it becomes a latency or operations burden.
scores.rationale: Identifies one-way points (write cutover, engine/vendor choice) with revisit triggers, reverse CDC exit and routing bypass; replatform to managed DB lock-in has a fallback.

scores.evidence: Keep the monolith as it is. A migration is not the time to re-architect.
scores.rationale: Mostly proportionate, avoiding rewrite; eight phases and 3 rehearsals plus 14-day gates are heavy but justified for a hospital.

scores.evidence: Tasks, in runbook order, in a low-volume window (e.g. Sunday 02:00): 1. Pause writes at the routing layer.
scores.rationale: Dependency-ordered phases with concrete tasks, checkable exit criteria, and revisit triggers; team can start from Phase 0 immediately.

checklist.evidence: BAA signed before any PHI moves. Private link only. PHI scrubbed from logs.
Every interface has been repointed to the cloud and back in a test environment.
Per-table row counts and checksums, nightly and on demand.
Exactly one database accepts bookings at any time, protected by a fencing mechanism.
Rollback completed in ≤ 15 min with zero lost bookings.
Add a second redundant private link, plus a site-to-site VPN as last-resort backup.
Paper downtime procedures and downtime report PCs refreshed and staged
Federate on-prem AD with Entra ID (or IAM Identity Center).
Load-test at 2× the recorded Monday 08:00 peak.
Retire on-prem storage under NIST 800-88 media sanitisation, with records-retention sign-off.

traps.evidence: At least 3 full rehearsals on a production-sized clone, including one rollback rehearsal.
Exactly one database accepts bookings at any time
Keep the monolith as it is.

note: Strong, disciplined replatform plan with explicit single-writer fencing, CDC, rehearsed rollback and interface inventory; weak on cost, cutover communication/hypercare, vendor licensing, and clinical downtime detail.
